materials.notes: Lattice: NBS 1955 powder value at 26 °C, converted to K by +273.15 (299.15 K). Other sources seen: P. A. Young, J. Phys. D 1, 936 (1968) abstract gives a0 = 3.1475 Å at 293 K for thin single crystals (https://api.openalex.org/works/doi:10.1088/0022-3727/1/7/416) - this disagrees with the NBS 3.1604 Å by 0.4% and is not used; Gan & Liu (arXiv:1608.08315) quote a = 3.160, c = 12.294 Å (Böker et al. 2001), consistent with NBS. Bulk modulus: the PDF text layer renders the values as 'K0T ¼ 53.471 GPa ... 9.270.4' (font-encoding garbling of '=' and '±'); the OSTI abstract renders it as K0T=53.4±1 GPa, K'=9.2±0.4. Aksoy used a methanol-ethanol medium (hydrostatic to ~10 GPa); no C33 or numeric axial compressibility was extracted. Thermal expansion: NO primary 300-1200 K values could be opened. El-Mahalawy & Evans (1976, the standard 20-800 °C XRD study) and Murray & Evans (1979, 10-320 K) are both closed-access and blocked; the only numbers seen are a secondary quote (see secondary_reported_unverified) with no assigned temperature. Gan & Liu also quote Murray & Evans (10-320 K) as αa = 4.922e-6, αc = 18.580e-6 /K, again without a stated T. TPRC Vol. 13 (Touloukian et al. 1977) lists only Young (1968) for MoS2 (a-axis, 78-374 K) under 'Miscellaneous Sulfides', without recommended values. A 2018 helium-diffraction study (Anemone et al., 2D Mater. 5, 035015) reports the surface in-plane lattice constant constant within error from 90-522 K (abstract), i.e. small alpha_a, but gives no coefficient. Debye temperature and melting point are secondary citations (primary sources closed); both are given as ranges with value=null.

materials.notes: Lattice: compilation (Ioffe) citing Lynch & Drickamer 1966 at 297 K; consistent with Ouyang et al. arXiv:1912.06187 Table 2 which lists Pease (1952) a = 2.50399(5), c = 6.6612(5) Å (https://arxiv.org/pdf/1912.06187). Muhammad et al. 2024 give 300 K values from the heating run of a0 = 2.5069(2), c0 = 6.6706(7) Å (Eqs. 1-2), about 0.1% larger than the consensus, and 2.504 / 6.661 Å as zero-pressure intercepts of their DAC run (Table 4); the formula block above uses their own a0/c0 so that relative expansion stays self-consistent. Thermal expansion: alpha values listed are instantaneous (1/L)(dL/dT) that I evaluated from the published fits (dividing by L/L0), so they are NOT the tabulated coefficients. Note in particular that the tabulated αa = −4.63e-6 is the linear coefficient of a cubic polynomial in T (not T−300), so the true αa at 300 K from the fit is −2.98e-6 /K. The c-axis fit is linear, so αc ≈ 42.3e-6 /K, decreasing slightly to 40.6e-6 /K at 1280 K only because of normalisation to c(T). Literature compared in Muhammad Table 1: Pease 273-1073 K αc = 40.5, αa = −2.9 (1e-6/K); Yates et al. (interferometry, 80-780 K) αc = 38.0, αa = −2.76; Zhao et al. 300-1280 K αc = 51.6 (outlier). Bulk modulus: literature values scatter widely (Muhammad Table 3): Solozhenko et al. 36.7±0.5 (K' 5.6, Murnaghan), Zhao et al. 17.6±0.8 (K' 19.5), Le Godec et al. 27.6±0.5 (K' 10.5); the helium-medium value 27.4 GPa is used. The Reuss (uniform-stress) bulk modulus 25.6 GPa is my calculation from the Bosak Cij: K_R = [(C11+C12)C33 − 2C13²]/(C11+C12+2C33−4C13). Linear compressibilities are my evaluation of −(1/x0)dx/dP at P = 0 from the Table 4 polynomials (B/A). Melting: Zhang, Guo, Xiao, He, Chinese J. High Pressure Phys. 38(6), 063401 (2024), doi:10.11858/gywlxb.20240813 (https://gywlxb.cn/cn/article/doi/10.11858/gywlxb.20240813): 'the melting points of h-BN under 3.4 and 4.3 GPa are (4251±150) K and (4531±200) K, respectively'. No sourced solid-state phase transition at ambient pressure; the h-BN to w-BN/c-BN conversions at high P/T were not sourced here. The TPRC Vol. 13 'recommended' BN expansion (Table 313R) applies to cubic BN specimens, so it is not used.

materials.notes: Lattice: Nelson & Riley give a, c in kX units at 14.6 °C; converted with 1 kX = 1.00202 Å (factor stated in NBS Circular 539 Vol. 5 introduction: 'd-spacings in kX units, using the factor 1.00202', https://nvlpubs.nist.gov/nistpubs/Legacy/circ/nbscircular539v5.pdf) -> a = 2.4612 Å, c = 6.7078 Å; T = 14.6 + 273.15 = 287.75 K (below the 295-300 K target; graphite c expands ~2.5e-5/K so c(298 K) is ~0.0017 Å larger). Cross-checks: Mohr et al. arXiv:0705.2418 (single-crystal flake XRD) a = 2.463, c = 6.712 Å (T not stated); Wang et al. 2012 a0 = 2.462(1), c0 = 6.721(2) Å from EOS fit; Ouyang Table 1 lists Lynch & Drickamer 2.4612 / 6.7078 Å. Bulk modulus: primary Hanfland paper is closed; value taken from Ouyang et al. Table 1 (that table misprints the Hanfland a0 as '2.603(4)'). Other experimental values in the same table: Lynch & Drickamer 32±2 (B' 12.3±0.7), Zhao & Spain 30.8±2. Wang et al. 2012 report K0 = 57.3(0.8) GPa but with K' fixed at 4, which is inappropriate for graphite (B' ~9), so not used; their K0a/K0c are Birch-Murnaghan-like fits to a^3 and c^3 (linear modulus ×3 convention), also with K' = 4. Reuss bulk modulus 36.4 GPa is my calculation from Bosak Cij: K_R = [(C11+C12)C33 − 2C13²]/(C11+C12+2C33−4C13); Voigt average (281.6 GPa) is meaningless for such anisotropy. Thermal expansion: TPRC values are for PYROLYTIC graphite (perpendicular / parallel to deposition plane), used as proxies for single-crystal c / a axes; they are 'provisional' (±10%) and alpha values are read directly from the TPRC table. Single-crystal reference values (Kirby et al. 1972 via Michigan Tech compilation) give a more negative αa (-1.2 vs -0.6 at 293 K) and higher αc (25.9 vs 23.1 at 293 K). Nelson & Riley 1945 abstract gives an average c-direction coefficient of 28.3e-6 over 15-800 °C (288-1073 K) (abstract text literally says 'for a', evidently a typo since a contracts) and states a contracts up to ~400 °C then expands slightly. Marsden et al. (Proc. R. Soc. A 2018, PMC6237503) quote a Nelson & Riley d-spacing fit, but as transcribed it does not reproduce c at room temperature, so it was not used.
